judged_text: `remove_member` uses `group.users.delete(user_id)` followed by `group.save`, which deletes the join row without executing GroupUser callbacks and does not recompute `group.user_count`. After a successful removal through this endpoint the group's denormalized `user_count` (displayed as `({{user_count}})` in the new admin template and used for pagination via `meta.total`) is stale until something else refreshes it, so the member pagination shows a wrong total and a phantom page.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims `user_count`/`meta.total` will be stale after `remove_member`, causing wrong pagination. But in this diff the client’s `removeMember` action calls `self.findMembers()` after the DELETE (see `discourse/models/group.js`), and `GroupsController#members` returns `meta.total` computed from `group.users.count` on every request (not from a denormalized `group.user_count` column). `findMembers()` then sets `user_count` from `result.meta.total`, so the admin template’s `({{user_count}})` and pagination inputs are refreshed immediately after removal.
